title: Risks and Controls for Multi-Agent Systems: an analytical framework for deployment of AI agents across organisational boundaries
abstract: arXiv:2608.26626v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This report presents a framework to help organisations, policymakers and researchers reason about the risks that emerge when AI agents interact with each other, how those risks change as interactions cross organisational boundaries, and the controls that may help address them.   As organisations deploy AI agents, those agents will increasingly interact with each other: inside the organisation, with the agents of partners, customers and suppliers, and with unknown counterparties on the open internet. Failures can emerge from the interactions themselves, and once those interactions cross an organisation's perimeter, no single organisation can fully see, control or govern them.   The report introduces three deployment tiers, defined by the minimum common governance binding any two interacting agents: singular governance, where one organisation governs every agent; federated governance, where multiple organisations deploy into a shared env

translated_title: 多智能体系统的风险与控制：跨组织边界部署AI智能体的分析框架
translated_abstract: 本报告提出了一个框架，帮助组织、政策制定者和研究人员思考AI智能体相互交互时出现的风险、这些风险如何随着交互跨越组织边界而变化，以及可能有助于应对这些风险的控制措施。随着组织部署AI智能体，这些智能体将越来越多地相互交互：在组织内部，与合作伙伴、客户和供应商的智能体交互，以及与开放互联网上未知对手方交互。失败可能源于交互本身，一旦这些交互跨越组织边界，任何单一组织都无法完全看到、控制或治理它们。报告介绍了三个部署层级，由约束任何两个交互智能体的最低共同治理定义：单一治理，即一个组织治理所有智能体；联邦治理，即多个组织部署到共享环境中。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个分析框架，通过定义三个部署层级（单一、联邦和开放治理）来系统评估多智能体系统跨组织交互时的风险，并强调跨边界交互中控制与治理的挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an analytical framework defining three deployment tiers (singular, federated, and open governance) to systematically assess risks in multi-agent systems across organizational boundaries, highlighting challenges of control and governance in cross-boundary interactions.
